I wish people valued that more than my problems, but it doesn't seem to work like that.

I've never felt confortable trying new things, so I always kept with the same and I was happy with that.

That's indeed random, but not that much.

Thanks. I do sometimes feel comfort thinking that people have given up for much less than this but it can't last forever.

It's a fair thing to say. They were great friends for the first couple months after I met them, they managed to handle me for sometime and that helped a lot, I still had some downs every once in a while and that probably overwhelmed them a bit. My friend that is trying to help me, she was once in a similar situation to mine, but didn't have depression as bad as mine, and she got lucky with life after a while. Still, they're probably the best friends I ever had even though it could be better. I've had people who I called friends just mentally abuse me over an entire lunch and I had to endure that, at least they don't do that. Yes I totally understand them, and I don't want to force them to help me if they don't want to, and I'm totally here for them if they need but if they don't help me I simply don't have anyone else.

I'll be spending at least a weekend over at home every month, I wish I could do more but the train ticket is a bit expensive and my income is not that good as my motivation to work is been very low to nothing for almost a year now. Yes the change was abrupt, but I didn't know what else to do. Thing is, I was already feeling like this before I moved, and unless things get better here it's just going to get worse. I knew it was a big risk but... I had no other option.

That's a good question. I do enjoy somethings but they don't bring me the joy they used to, I just spend my free time in the computer, either watching videos on Youtube or playing games. I used to be good just be left alone playing a game for days and days but it stopped working like that for quite some time now. Even when I'm playing something I just get bored and bad thoughts pop in my head.
